acceptanceCriteria: Inventory returns every bound Stripe credential class with mode, application/resource scope, permissions, owner, fingerprint, status, generation, and verification time
Inventory, API responses, logs, receipts, and database rows contain no key or webhook-secret values
Test and live bindings are distinct and cross-mode fallback or reuse fails
The adapter rejects application mappings broader than the approved permission manifest and reports why
Webhook signing-secret rotation cannot be authorized by a restricted API-key grant
userStories.description: Implement a generic Stripe AuthorityProviderAdapter and ProviderBinding inventory for account, test/live mode, application/resource binding, key kind, permission manifest, owner, fingerprint, SecretStore reference, target-binding reference, status, binding generation, and last verification. Treat webhook signing secrets as a distinct credential class. Use core tables/routes and no provider-specific secret column or child migration. Never map application runtime to an unrestricted account secret when a restricted key can satisfy the declared operations.
userStories.title: Stripe bindings inventory least-privilege credentials without storing values

acceptanceCriteria: Changing permissions, mode, target, canary, grace, rollback, or current fingerprint changes the digest and invalidates approval
Required Dashboard reauthentication and restricted-key creation cannot be bypassed, scripted through model prompts, or marked complete without provider evidence
Secure operator capture writes the replacement to SecretStore/target binding and returns only reference, fingerprint, and provenance
A replacement broader than the approved permission manifest or in the wrong mode is rejected before cutover
Waiting for the human step does not consume story timeout and resumes exactly once against the same intent
userStories.description: Define an immutable rotation intent with current fingerprint, exact restricted permission manifest, test/live mode, target binding, canary, grace period, rollback, and human-step requirements. When Stripe Dashboard reauthentication or manual creation is required, pause in WAITING_FOR_AUTHENTICATION and present a secure operator ceremony. Capture the replacement directly into SecretStore/target binding; the model and ordinary API never receive it. Do not automate MFA, bypass provider controls, or use an unrestricted account secret as replacement.
userStories.title: Human-assisted restricted-key creation bypasses neither reauthentication nor secret isolation

acceptanceCriteria: The old key remains active while secure capture, target stage, canary, and post-cutover verification are pending
The canary calls a real Stripe test-mode operation requiring the declared permissions rather than only a local health endpoint
Grace-period state records both fingerprints and exact expiry without exposing either value
Old-key revocation occurs only after successful canary/cutover and is followed by verified old-key rejection
Replay or crash discovers the existing replacement/binding state and produces no duplicate rotation or untracked key
userStories.description: Stage the replacement through RuntimeSecretBindingAdapter, run a real bounded Stripe test-mode operation matching the permission manifest, verify target health and fingerprint, then enter the declared grace period. After post-cutover verification, revoke the old key through the supported provider/human ceremony and verify old-key failure. Reconcile provider and target state before retrying uncertain steps.
userStories.title: Verified canary and grace cut over before old-key revocation

acceptanceCriteria: Canary or pre-revocation failure restores the prior binding, retains the old key, quarantines the replacement, and records a rollback receipt
Runtime authentication failure creates a typed emergency request linked to binding, fingerprint, evidence, and affected resource without a secret
Emergency state cannot grant itself, broaden permissions, cross mode/workspace, or skip required Dashboard authentication
Unknown old/new key status is read back or sent to manual reconciliation before retry
Errors, incident evidence, receipts, WAL events, and UI contain no Stripe key or webhook-secret value
userStories.description: Implement failure and runtime-detection paths. Canary/cutover failure restores the prior target binding, keeps the old key active when safe, quarantines the replacement, and emits a rollback receipt. Revoked/failing runtime credentials create a structured emergency rotation request with evidence; they do not inject a new secret or bypass approval. Unknown revocation outcome is reconciled before another action.
userStories.title: Rotation failure restores payment access and surfaces emergency authority

acceptanceCriteria: The test-mode journey proves restricted permissions, secure capture, real canary, cutover, and rollback without exposing key values
Prompt extraction, cross-mode/workspace use, broadened permissions, altered intent, replay, and expired grant all fail
Crash at secure capture, target stage, canary, grace, revocation, and receipt settlement resumes or reconciles once
Every injected failure leaves the prior disposable payment binding functional or records an explicit manual-reconciliation blocker
No Categoric/Cashflow-App Stripe account, key, environment, payment flow, or product code is used
userStories.description: Qualify on a dedicated Rorca-owned Stripe test account and disposable target binding. Exercise least-privilege inventory, human-assisted capture, real canary, grace, revocation verification where supported, rollback, runtime failure, replay, cross-mode/workspace denial, prompt extraction, and crash recovery. Live-mode remains disabled until separately authorized evidence exists. Rollback disables the adapter, restores the prior target binding, revokes/quarantines replacements, and preserves receipts. Non-goals are payment-product changes, billing logic, webhook processing, customer accounts, and automatic provider-control bypass.
userStories.title: Stripe test-mode attacks cannot expose keys or interrupt the prior binding
